\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{معاینه} \fa{کردن} (mo'âyene kardan)}{معاینه کردن (mo'âyene kardan)}]{\fa{معاینه} \fa{کردن} (mo'âyene kardan) — to examine (a patient)}

\label{lesson:FA-C493-moayene-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to feel faint, then the Persian for to sweat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{معاینه} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{معاینه} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{mo'âyene kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to examine (a patient)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دکتر} \fa{گلوی} \fa{او} \fa{را} \fa{معاینه} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{doktor galu-ye u râ mo'âyene kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor examined her throat.
\end{quote}

\emph{mo'âyene} 'medical examination' + \emph{kardan}; present stem \emph{kon-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mo'âyene} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{muʿāyana}, 'inspection, seeing with one's eyes'. EtymDB has no entry for it. \emph{kardan} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mo'âyene kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mo'âyene kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mo'âyene kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to feel faint, then the Persian for to sweat, then say \emph{mo'âyene kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{معاینه} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To examine (a patient)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نبض} (nabz)}{نبض (nabz)}]{\fa{نبض} (nabz) — pulse}

\label{lesson:FA-C493-nabz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to sweat, then the Persian for to examine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نبض}}
\textbf{\fa{نبض}} (\emph{nabz}) — \textquotedblleft{}pulse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پرستار} \fa{نبض} \fa{بیمار} \fa{را} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{parastâr nabz-e bimâr râ gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The nurse took the patient's pulse.
\end{quote}

\emph{nabz gereftan} — to take a pulse.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nabz} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{nabḍ}, 'pulse' (EtymDB). EtymDB takes Urdu and Hindi \emph{nabz} from the same Arabic word (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nabz}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to sweat, then the Persian for to examine, then say \emph{nabz} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{درمان} \fa{کردن} (darmân kardan)}{درمان کردن (darmân kardan)}]{\fa{درمان} \fa{کردن} (darmân kardan) — to treat (an illness)}

\label{lesson:FA-C493-darman-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to examine, then the Persian for pulse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{درمان} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{درمان} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{darmân kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to treat (an illness)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{دکتر} \fa{بیماری} \fa{پوست} \fa{را} \fa{درمان} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in doktor bimâri-ye pust râ darmân mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This doctor treats skin disease.
\end{quote}

\emph{darmân} 'cure, treatment' + \emph{kardan}. \emph{darmângâh} 'clinic' is built on the same noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{darmân} is inherited: EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian, where it meant 'remedy, medicine' (EtymDB). \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{واکسن} \fa{زدن} (vâksan zadan)}{واکسن زدن (vâksan zadan)}]{\fa{واکسن} \fa{زدن} (vâksan zadan) — to get vaccinated; to vaccinate}

\label{lesson:FA-C493-vaksan-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for pulse, then the Persian for to treat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{واکسن} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{واکسن} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{vâksan zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to get vaccinated; to vaccinate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{در} \fa{مدرسه} \fa{واکسن} \fa{زدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchehâ dar madrese vâksan zadand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children had their jabs at school.
\end{quote}

\emph{vâksan} 'vaccine' + \emph{zadan} 'to strike'. It covers both giving and getting a jab.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vâksan} is a modern loan, usually traced to French \emph{vaccin}, 'vaccine'. EtymDB has no entry for it. \emph{zadan}, 'to strike', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چکاپ} (chekâp)}{چکاپ (chekâp)}]{\fa{چکاپ} (chekâp) — a check-up}

\label{lesson:FA-C493-chekap}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to treat, then the Persian for to get vaccinated.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چکاپ}}
\textbf{\fa{چکاپ}} (\emph{chekâp}) — \textquotedblleft{}a check-up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{هر} \fa{سال} \fa{یک} \fa{چکاپ} \fa{کامل} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u har sâl yek chekâp-e kâmel mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He has a full check-up every year.
\end{quote}

\emph{chekâp kardan} — to have a check-up.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{chekâp} is a modern loan, usually traced to English \emph{check-up}. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
